explanation: The pole fires on content-bearing tokens of expository/reference prose: numerals, dates, ordinals and quantities (' six', ' twenty', ' 2009', ' 27', ' third', 'hundreds', 'percent'), place and person names (' France', ' Canada', ' India', 'Sanchez', ' Livingston'), spatial and measurement words (' north', ' toward', 'direction', ' side', 'thickness', 'density'), technical or scientific nouns ('devices', 'technologies', 'methods', 'types', 'particles', 'experiment') and the reporting or study verbs that present findings ('showed', 'announced', 'reported', 'demonstrate', 'indicate', 'revealed'); it also peaks on the word-final subword piece of a multi-token name or on a LaTeX or math symbol ('nu', ' dx', 'quad', '\{'), and in the scan roughly 40-47% of tokens in these classes clear the activity line against 16% of all tokens. It stays below the line on articles, pronouns and conjunctions ('the', 'a', 'of', 'and', 'he', 'she', 'we', 'it' - only 3% of determiner tokens are active) and on everyday concrete or narrative nouns ('food', 'fear', 'life', 'woman', 'war', 'room').
